subject.title: [Bug]: claude-cli backend SIGKILLs entire process tree at turn end — Workflow / background tool orphans have no opt-out

question: Should claude-cli live-session cleanup remain unconditional at turn end, or should OpenClaw add a bounded drain or telemetry contract for in-flight CLI-owned background grandchildren?
rationale: The source confirms the reported cleanup path, but changing it affects orphan prevention, process-tree cleanup guarantees, model-visible terminal state, and likely config/default behavior.

options.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
options.body: Add a narrow owner-approved contract for detecting in-flight CLI-owned background children, deferring cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surfacing forced cleanup to the parent session.

options.title: Telemetry first
options.body: Keep unconditional cleanup for now, but snapshot, log, or surface killed grandchildren so the silent failure class becomes observable before changing lifecycle behavior.

options.title: Keep cleanup as the contract
options.body: Document that Claude CLI Workflow or Bash grandchildren are not supported across turn boundaries and route users to OpenClaw exec/process or durable task surfaces instead.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
recommendation.body: Add a narrow owner-approved contract for detecting in-flight CLI-owned background children, deferring cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surfacing forced cleanup to the parent session.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus has the strongest recent history on Claude live-session behavior and is closest to the lifecycle contract being decided.
